channel.title: Mathematical Physics Lab — Frontier Radar — 数理物理
channel.description: 数学・数学のためのAI・基礎物理学の最先端を、arXiv の全数学分野と高エネルギー物理の新着、キーワード別に数年分さかのぼった arXiv 検索、最上位の学術誌、一流研究者のブログ、主要な賞の報道からまるごと集め、重要度で順位づけする検索型RSSリーダー。

item.title: Black hole binary mergers in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity with regularisation
item.description: We study the non-linear dynamics of Chern-Simons gravity with numerical relativity for the first time. We use the regularisation prescription to obtain a well-posed initial-value formulation in the gauges commonly used in numerical relativity, and we simulate head-on collisions and binary black hole mergers in the regime of validity of effective field theory, extracting the corresponding scalar and gravitational waves. This opens up the possibility to test general effective field theories of gravity, including… — Llibert Areste Salo, Maxence Corman, Pau Figueras, Aron D. Kovacs, Shunhui Yao — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO / arXiv hep-th

item.title: Orbit-averaged spinning and eccentric binary black holes: Hamiltonian and integrability
item.description: For over two decades, the orbit-averaged precession equations of spinning binary black holes at second post-Newtonian order have been a standard model for their spin dynamics. One of their constants of motion, the projected effective spin, underlies the stability analysis of aligned-spin configurations and the construction of analytical solutions. The system is known to be Hamiltonian and integrable, its Hamiltonian being the orbit average of the full post-Newtonian Hamiltonian. Independently, we derive this… — Tom Colin, Sashwat Tanay, Manuel Alva-Morales, Prateek Anand — arXiv gr-qc / astro-ph.CO

item.title: Forward Self-similar Solutions of the Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations in Dimensions Five and Higher
item.description: We construct forward self-similar solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 5$) for arbitrary $(-1)$-homogeneous, divergence-free initial data $u_0$ smooth on the unit sphere. For $n\ge 6$, the $O(|y|^{-3})$ bound on the nonlinear residual of the linear heat profile no longer yields $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$-integrability, obstructing a direct global energy perturbation around $e^Δu_0$. To overcome this difficulty, we truncate $u_0$ near the origin via a divergence-free cutoff… — Baishun Lai, Ruiyi Zhang, Xiaoxin Zheng — arXiv: navier

item.title: Extremal Projectors and the Virasoro Algebra
item.description: Extremal projectors are universal operators projecting onto the highest weight space in a representation. Their existence and uniqueness (as formal series) are known for a broad range of Lie superalgebras and quantum groups. We consider a class of Lie superalgebras that contains reductive finite-dimensional Lie algebras as well as the Virasoro algebra. We prove the existence and uniqueness of an extremal projector for this class. The existence proof is given in terms of a recursive algorithm which can be used to… — Jonas T. Hartwig, Sagar Shrivastava — arXiv math-ph / nlin.SI / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
item.description: The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute $SO(5)$ CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector $φ$, singlet $s$, and traceless symmetric scalar $t$, we… — Zhijin Li, Tinghong Shen — arXiv: bootstrap

item.title: On the thermal behavior of composites embedding extended general interfaces
item.description: In heterogeneous materials, surface roughness, chemical incompatibility, mechanical mismatch or manufacturing defects result in imperfect bonding between the constituents. Such imperfections introduce a finite-thickness interphase zone between the constituents that possess a graded or inhomogeneous micro-structure. It is virtually impossible to resolve the behavior of such interphases. Instead, a well-established approach is to replace the interphase by a zero-thickness interface endowed with its own energetic… — Soheil Firooz, Kashish Veda Eluri, Ali Javili, Paul Steinmann — arXiv math-ph / nlin.SI

item.title: Boundary dualities of symplectic Chern-Simons theories and minimal models
item.description: We propose that a Neumann-type boundary condition of the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ $USp(2n)$ Chern-Simons theory at the level $-(n+\frac32)$ with a fundamental chiral multiplet is dual to a Dirichlet-type boundary condition of an Abelian rank-$0$ theory. In a topological twist we propose that it supports the affine vertex operator algebra (VOA) $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2))$. With the corresponding specialization of the fugacities, the line defect half-indices of the antisymmetric Wilson lines give, up to monomials, the… — Yu Nakayama, Tadashi Okazaki — arXiv: hodge / arXiv: tqft

item.title: Vector bundles on spin Kähler surfaces and the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations
item.description: We compute new lower bounds on the second Chern class of a vector bundle $\mathscr{E}$ on a spin Kähler surface $X$ that satisfies $c_1(\mathscr{E}) = 0$ and $H^2(\text{End}_0\mathscr{E}) = 0.$ When $X$ is a regular elliptic surface and $\mathscr{E}$ has rank 2, our bound is sharp. Our technique is to use Furuta's finite-dimensional approximation on the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations, together with their algebro-geometric interpretation by the second named author. We also use these techniques to prove an… — Minh Lam Nguyen, Ollie Thakar — arXiv: low dim

item.title: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
item.description: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how… — Jie Gu — arXiv: hodge

item.title: Differential equations for twisted intertwining operators in abelian orbifold conformal field theory
item.description: Let $ V $ be a vertex operator algebra with two commuting automorphisms $ g_1 $ and $ g_2 $ (possibly of infinite order and non-semisimple). We derive a Jacobi identity for a twisted intertwining operator $ \mathcal{Y} $ of type $ \left( \begin{smallmatrix} W_3\\ W_1 \, W_2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) $ when $ W_1 $ is a $ g_1 $-twisted $ V $-module, $ W_2 $ is a $ g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module, and $ W_3 $ is a $ g_1 g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module. For any abelian group $ G $ of automorphisms of a CFT-type vertex operator… — Daniel Tan — arXiv: tqft

item.title: Almost complex structures on triple blow-ups
item.description: We show that for certain smooth 4-manifolds, almost complex structures on its triple blow-up induce all its spin$^c$ structures with a non-negative-dimensional Seiberg-Witten moduli space. Since this includes all basic classes, our result provides an approximation to the simple type conjecture. Moreover, we expand a result by Dieter Kotschick showing that every finitely presented group is the fundamental group of an almost complex 4-manifold. We show that it can furthermore be chosen to have every even integer as… — Samuel Adrian Antz — arXiv: low dim

item.title: Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
item.description: We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $γ\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $γ$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with… — Stavros Garoufalidis, Danylo Radchenko, Campbell Wheeler — arXiv: modularity / arXiv: riemann

item.title: P-curvature from a TQFT viewpoint
item.description: This paper is motivated by the recent discovery, in symplectic topology, of a relation (partly proved, partly conjectural) between quantum connection and quantum Steenrod operations. We introduce an abstract TQFT framework, based on certain features of the definition of deformed symplectic cohomology, in which such a relation holds generally. — Paul Seidel — arXiv: floer

item.title: Conformal field theory from automorphic forms on a quantum group
item.description: We reformulate two-dimensional conformal field theory (2d CFT) in the language of noncommutative geometry. To this end, we introduce automorphic forms for the von Neumann algebraic quantum group $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. A quantum measure space is a von Neumann algebra equipped with a weight. We study such spaces carrying a weight-preserving action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. We argue that every unitary bosonic 2d CFT with central charge $c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2>1$ is equivalent to a quantum measure… — Dalimil Mazac — arXiv: bootstrap

item.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
item.description: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution… — Oliver O'Brien, Atsushi Ueda, Etienne Granet, Henrik Dreyer, Frank Verstraete — arXiv: gen sym

item.title: More physics at the entangling surface: boundary conditions and entanglement in 2d TQFT
item.description: We present a systematic treatment of entanglement in two-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). Our approach clarifies the sensitivity of entanglement measures to the cutting maps that implement Hilbert space factorization. Such maps embed the TQFT Hilbert space into a description with potentially more degrees of freedom, and for entanglement to be well defined they must be isometric, i.e., they must preserve the norms of all states. We show that the naïve cutting map based solely upon path… — Jackson R. Fliss, Alan Rios Fukelman, Stathis Vitouladitis — arXiv: gen sym / arXiv: tqft

item.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
item.description:
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from… — Fedor K. Popov, Leonardo Rastelli — arXiv: lean / arXiv: modularity / arXiv: tqft

item.title: Multipartite Entanglement, TQFT Partition Functions and PL Bordism
item.description: In a previous work we conjectured that the multi-invariants of the ground state of a gapped $(d-1)+1$-dimensional system, labeled by bipartite $(d+1)$-edge-colored graphs encoding closed oriented $d$-manifolds $M$, compute the partition functions $Z(M)$ of the low energy topological quantum field theory (TQFT), up to non-universal factors determined by the local structure of the triangulation. In this paper we determine which combinations of partition functions can be isolated from the non-universal factors. The… — Michele Del Zotto, Abhijit Gadde, Pavel Putrov — arXiv: tqft

item.title: On Entanglement Dynamics in Holographic Theories
item.description: Entanglement entropy (EE) is central to modern theoretical physics, yet its calculation in interacting theories with nontrivial time dependence remains challenging. In this thesis, we investigate the real-time dynamics of EE in strongly coupled quantum field theories (QFTs) using the Anti-de Sitter/Conformal Field Theory (AdS/CFT) correspondence. We first examine EE evolution in an exactly solvable two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT) with an inhomogeneous sine-square deformation (SSD). We argue that the… — Hanzhi Jiang — arXiv: ads cft

item.title: An Explicit Construction of Commuting Quantum KdV Hamiltonians in the Universal Virasoro Vertex Algebra
item.description: We give an explicit formula for elements $H_{2k}$ of conformal weight $2k$, $k\ge1$, in the universal Virasoro vertex operator algebra $V$ at every central charge, such that $H_{2k}(0)H_{2l}\in TV$ for all $k,l\ge1$. Modulo translation, the kernel of $H_4(0)$ is generated by $[H_{2k}]$ in each positive even weight and is zero in positive odd weights. The formula uses a realization on differential polynomials by possibly infinite-order differential operators in a completion of the Weyl algebra, together with the… — Hongbo Zhao — arXiv: tqft

item.title: Edge dynamics of covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons
item.description: We study the covariant higher-rank Chern-Simons theory of fractons in 2+1 dimensions in the presence of a planar boundary. The differential generator associated with the scalar gauge symmetry singles out a single scalar Ward combination of the functional field equations. Its zeroth and first normal moments give two integrated boundary identities. The zeroth moment yields a traceless rank-two current obeying a fractonic double-divergence conservation law and a higher-rank Kac-Moody algebra. The first moment makes… — Erica Bertolini, Matteo Carrega, Nicola Maggiore, Daniel Sacco Shaikh, Maria Florencia Semino — arXiv: kakeya

item.title: Summing over Seifert Manifolds in Narain Ensemble Averages
item.description: The ensemble average of Narain conformal field theories over their moduli space is a real-analytic Eisenstein series, whose Poincaré expansion can be interpreted as a sum over lens spaces weighted by the partition functions of Abelian Chern-Simons theory. In this paper we extend this correspondence from lens spaces to Seifert manifolds, which gives an example of a restricted sum over topologies of the kind that arises in three-dimensional quantum gravity. A Seifert manifold is obtained from a fixed core, a… — Kei Kaneda, Masahito Yamazaki — arXiv: modularity

item.title: The Virasoro Bootstrap: from the $c\sim1$ desert to coupled Potts
item.description: We develop a numerical conformal bootstrap for two-dimensional CFTs with $c>1$ based on Virasoro conformal blocks, computed with Zamolodchikov's recursion and optimal polynomial interpolation. As a first test we isolate an island around three decoupled Ising models. We then consider three 3-state Potts models coupled through their energy operators, a candidate irrational CFT. Mixed correlators isolate the decoupled theory in an island, and different gap assumptions, motivated by perturbation theory, yield a… — Stefanos R. Kousvos, Alessandro Piazza, Alessandro Vichi — arXiv: bootstrap / arXiv: kakeya

item.title: Statistical mechanics and hierarchy of learnability in quantum codes: From generalized symmetries to non-Abelian topological orders
item.description: Local weak measurements provide noisy information about observables encoded in a quantum code. We formulate the corresponding Bayesian inference problem for a broad class of topological stabilizer codes by mapping it to classical spin models with generalized symmetries. When the wavefunction deformation and Gaussian measurement strengths coincide, the replicated model acquires an enlarged symmetry. We use this symmetry to derive exact identities among correlators averaged over measurement records that quantify… — Hiromi Ebisu, Masazumi Honda — arXiv: gen sym

item.title: A Sojourn Through $c=1$ String Theory
item.description: We revisit the $S$-matrix, the thermal $S$-matrix and the thermal free energy of $c=1$ string theory from the worldsheet perspective. By numerically integrating Virasoro conformal blocks with DOZZ structure constants, we compute the scattering amplitudes and thermal amplitudes up to 6-point at tree level and up to 3-point at one loop, in addition to the genus two thermal free energy. All results are in agreement with the predicted answers from the $c=1$ matrix model. — Sam Christian, Yuchen Wang, Xi Yin, Yutai Zhang — arXiv: amplitudes

item.title: Higher Integrability, Generalized Symmetries, and Partially Topological Field Theories
item.description: We exhibit a classical link between higher Lax integrability and generalized symmetries in a non-Lorentzian higher semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory on $M\times\mathbb CP^1$. The equations of motion determine a spectrally dependent flat higher connection on $M$ whose Laurent coefficients organise an infinite hierarchy of conserved quantities. We construct a spectral family of classical $(d_M-2)$-form symmetry line defects associated with the Lax connection, establish an action-preserving deformation law, and… — Luigi Alfonsi, Leron Borsten, Mehran Jalali Farahani, Hyungrok Kim, Martin Wolf, Charles A. S. Young — arXiv: gen sym

item.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlevé Equation
item.description: For the first Painlevé equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_π\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-π}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes… — Kohei Iwaki, Noam Tamarin — arXiv: modularity

item.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
item.description: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For… — Zixuan Feng, Zhengwei Liu — arXiv: tqft

item.title: What crossing symmetry forbids just above $c=1$
item.description: What does a unitary two-dimensional conformal field theory look like just above $c=1$? Using the numerical conformal bootstrap, we study the four-point function of a scalar Virasoro primary $φ$ such that no primary lighter than $φ$ appears in its operator product expansion with itself. Slightly above $c=1$, crossing symmetry excludes the interval $0.17\lesssimΔ_φ\lesssim1$, although the compact boson realizes every such $Δ_φ$ at $c=1$. Combining this exclusion with results from the modular bootstrap, we show that… — Yu Nakayama — arXiv: bootstrap / arXiv: modularity

item.title: Ricci flow of Integrable Sigma Models, Hitchin Systems and Quantum Seiberg-Witten theory
item.description: We construct a family of integrable 2d sigma models through 4d Chern-Simons theory and show that their classical point-particle reduction corresponds to a Hitchin system. The integrable Hitchin quantisation then provides a natural candidate Hamiltonian for the one-loop reduced dynamics of the sigma models, which coincides with the Perelman operator in all cases examined. This allows us to study the corresponding spectral problems using 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theory and 2d conformal field theory methods. For the… — G. Bonelli, S. Lacroix, T. Pedroni, A. Tanzini — arXiv: ricci

item.title: On the direct SLE-martingale approach to the integrability of Conformal Loop Ensembles
item.description: This paper is about the derivation of "integrability results" (i.e., for example, explicit formulas for the probability of events involving a few marked points) for Conformal Loop Ensembles, that are the (conjectured) scaling limits of discrete crititical planar lattice models from Statistical Physics. We discuss the explicit solutions to the PDEs provided by the original SLE/CLE martingale approach that AI now makes it possible to uncover. This provides short and direct new proofs of a number of formulas that… — Jason Miller, Wendelin Werner — arXiv: sle

item.title: Generalized Symmetries of QED$_4$ on Non-Spin Manifolds
item.description: Generalized symmetries are sensitive to the tangential structure of spacetime. We study this interplay for massless QED on oriented non-spin four-manifolds, where the photon becomes a spin$^c$ connection and the path integral sums over spin$^c$ structures. The shifted flux quantization extends the magnetic 1-form symmetry into a $w_2$-twisted 1-form symmetry: its $2π$ rotation acts as a gravitational sign, fixed by the normal bundle of the surface the operator wraps. The obstruction to treating it as an ordinary… — Michele Del Zotto, Vivek Saxena — arXiv: gen sym

item.title: Crossed modularity of twisted VOA modules
item.description: Let $V$ be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and $G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ a finite group. Using the $G$-crossed braided fusion structure of twisted modules constructed in \cite{Crossed}, we prove that the conformal twist $e^{2πiL(0)}$ gives a crossed ribbon structure and that the crossed category is modular in Kirillov's sense. Consequently, its equivariantization is a modular tensor category. We also obtain dimension and simple-object counting formulas for the twisted sectors. — Shun Xu — arXiv: modularity / arXiv: tqft

item.title: Equivalence between rationality and modular invariance under $C_2$-cofiniteness
item.description: We prove that for a simple and $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, the rationality is equivalent to the modular invariance of the space of complete ordinary one-point trace functions of its irreducible modules. This proves a conjecture given by Dong-Ren in \cite{DongRen}, which is also the inverse theorem of Zhu's modular invariance theorem \cite{Zhu}. — Hao Wang, Jiang Yang — arXiv: modularity / arXiv: tqft

item.title: On generators and relations for $O_n^irc(V)$ in higher-level Zhu algebras, Part II
item.description: We study circle relations in the higher-level Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra $V$. For regular vacuum words in homogeneous letters, we prove the termwise correction-residue conjecture of Part I: every correction in the one-sided iterate expansion belongs separately to the finite-length plus subspace. The first correction formed with the left truncated field vanishes identically. Multiplying the diagonal commutator kernel by a power of $1+x$ turns it into a Laurent polynomial. This proves the vanishing… — Nathan P Vander Werf — arXiv: tqft

item.title: A Five-Dimensional Nonassociative Algebra: elliptic integrability and bracketing-dependent dynamics
item.description: We introduce a five-dimensional nonassociative real algebra $\mathbb{P}$ whose one-generated subalgebras are complex while its left, middle, and right nuclei are all $\mathbb{R}$. This contrast permits an unambiguous one-element functional calculus but makes polynomial ordinary differential equations sensitive to bracketing. We classify the homogeneous quadratic words containing one fixed coefficient $B$ and two copies of $p$ that preserve $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\{1,B,p\}$. For a fixed-coefficient… — Alireza Poshtkohi, Susanne Pumpluen — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Viscosity variation in fluid flows across scales
item.description: Author(s): Arjun Sharma, Ritabrata Thakur, Sharath Jose, and Rama Govindarajan Although most treatments of fluid mechanics consider the fluid viscosity to be constant or uniform, many systems have a viscosity that varies in time or space. Examples arise in microbial habitats, in the ocean, and in Earth’s mantle. In this review, the authors explain how viscosity gradients occur in real systems, examine how these gradients lead to new phenomena at both low and high Reynolds number, and highlight open research… — Arjun Sharma, Ritabrata Thakur, Sharath Jose, Rama Govindarajan — Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 045002 (2026) / Reviews of Modern Physics

item.title: Vertex operator algebra realizations of untwisted Haagerup--Izumi centers
item.description: For every odd integer $N\geq3$, we construct an untwisted Haagerup--Izumi fusion category $\mathcal H_N$ on the negative spherical branch and a simple, self-contragredient, regular, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra $E_N$ of central charge $-16N$, together with an equivalence of modular fusion categories: \[ \operatorname{Rep}(E_N)\simeq Z(\mathcal H_N). \] The VOA $E_N$ is rational, has exactly $N^2+3$ irreducible modules, and is lower bounded and integer graded, with least conformal degree $-(N-1)/2$. The… — David E. Evans, Andrew Riesen — arXiv: modularity / arXiv: tqft

item.title: The Free Scalar as a Thermal Envelope for Three-Dimensional CFTs
item.description: We conjecture that every unitary three-dimensional conformal field theory obeys $c_S/C_T\leq16πζ(3)$, where $s=c_ST^2$ is the thermal entropy density and $C_T$ the stress-tensor two-point coefficient, with equality for free scalars. We embed this in a stronger conjecture: on $S^1\times H^2$, the $C_T$-normalized hyperbolic heat capacity is bounded above by that of the free scalar for all $T\geq(2πR)^{-1}$. Near the conformal temperature, for theories smooth from the high-temperature side and without boundary… — Christopher P. Herzog, Andreas Stergiou — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Towards a Complete Kerr Soft-Hair Theory: Integrability, Counterterm Equivalence,and Quantum State Counting
item.description: The horizon symmetry construction of Haco, Hawking, Perry, and Strominger yield two Virasoro central charges 12J after a specified Wald-Zoupas correction. Turning that calculation into a black hole microstate theory requires separate control of nonlinear charge integrability, the allowed counter-term class, and quantum state multiplicities. We formulate exact local and global integrability tests, prove uniqueness of the counter-term coefficients within a one-parameter ansatz, and identify the quotient in which a… — Sandi Setiawan — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Quantum-Seeded Distributed Post-Quantum Group Signatures for 5G V2X Communications
item.description: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications rely on elliptic-curve signatures that a quantum adversary breaks and on pseudonym certificates whose anonymity rests on rotation rate, not cryptography. This work presents qDGSP, a post-quantum V2X infrastructure: a hash-based dynamic group signature scheme (DGSP, over SPHINCS+ and WOTS+) distributed between a central controller and roadside verifiers. Group keys derive deterministically from quantum key distribution (QKD) seeds served over the ETSI GS QKD 014… — P. Blanco-Casal, P. Rejo-Iglesias, D. Cajaraville-Aboy, J. Vecino-Peñas, R. P. Díaz-Redondo, A. Fernández-Vilas — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: A Topological Quantum Field Theory for Representation Varieties of Torus Links
item.description: We construct a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) that computes the virtual classes of $G$-representation varieties associated with the fundamental group of a torus link complement. Following the framework established by González-Prieto, Logares and Muñoz for $G$-representation varieties of surface groups, we introduce a suitable bordism whose iteration enables a recursive topological evaluation of these virtual classes. Via this TQFT, we explicitly compute the virtual class of these varieties for the groups… — Enrique Aycart-Maldonado, Alejandro Calleja — arXiv: tqft

item.title: Random Euclidean CFT$_2$ from Triangulated dS$_3$ Gravity
item.description: We propose a random Euclidean CFT description of three-dimensional de Sitter gravity with fixed central charge and primary spectrum but fluctuating OPE coefficients. A normalized four-point coefficient extracted from the complex Liouville cosmological wavefunction matches the analytically continued tetrahedral Virasoro graph amplitude. Its two-copy form gives a non-Gaussian OPE correlation, with a modular $S$ transform relating the corresponding amplitude to fixed-angle Conformal Turaev--Viro theory. The $K_4$… — Ji-seong Chae — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Exact spectral integrability of a finite-channel random Schrödinger operator: from fermionization of the Dyson--Riccati gas to Kontsevich integral
item.description: We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schrödinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $β=2$ unitary symmetry class. The associated Dyson--Riccati eigenvalue gas admits an exact free-fermion representation at any sample length $L$, which in the limit $L\to \infty$ expresses the density of states and the total Lyapunov growth rate exactly through a single Airy Hankel $τ$-function providing multichannel generalization… — Yan V. Fyodorov, Pierre Le Doussal — arXiv: random matrix

item.title: $G$-crossed braided tensor categories of twisted modules
item.description: Let $V$ be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and $G\leq\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ a finite group. We prove Huang's conjecture that the categories of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, for $g\in G$, form a $G$-crossed braided fusion category. This category is faithfully $G$-graded, with tensor products representing the complete twisted intertwining operators of Du-Huang, the canonical pullback $G$-action, and crossed braiding. In particular, the associativity, coherence and rigidity required by the conjecture all hold. — Shun Xu — arXiv: tqft

item.title: A vertex operator algebra for the S-fold realisation of a non-unitary Haagerup--Izumi modular fusion category
item.description: We show that there exists a strongly rational vertex operator algebra $V_{11}$, proposed by Flohr, whose representation theory $\mathrm{Rep}\,V_{11}\simeq\mathrm{Sem}\otimes\mathcal Z(σ_2\mathcal F)$ as braided categories. Here $\mathrm{Sem}$ is the semion category (with the spherical structure in which its generator has dimension $-1$), $\mathcal F$ is Ostrik's twisted Haagerup category and $σ_2$ is the Galois automorphism $ζ_{117}\mapstoζ_{117}^2$. — David E Evans — arXiv: modularity / arXiv: tqft

item.title: Liouvillian Non-Invertible Symmetry
item.description: Non-invertible symmetries extend conventional symmetries beyond group-like transformations and play an important role in quantum field theory and many-body physics. However, a general framework of non-invertible symmetries in open quantum systems is still lacking. Here, we formulate a general Liouville-space duality framework that extends Hilbert-space non-invertible dualities to open quantum systems. The resulting defect relates Liouvillians with dual Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters and becomes an exact… — Ying-Cheng Yang, Jhen-Dong Lin, Yueh-Nan Chen — arXiv: gen sym

item.title: Froggatt-Nielsen mechanism with non-invertible symmetry
item.description: We formulate the Froggatt-Nielsen mechanism in the framework of non-invertible symmetries obtained by $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauging of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ or $U(1)$. While the non-invertible selection rules can constrain the texture-zero structure of fermion mass matrices, they do not by themselves determine the magnitudes of the allowed couplings. Introducing a flavon field allows the fusion rules to fix the leading powers of the small parameter $\varepsilon=\langle S\rangle/Λ$, thereby determining both the texture zeros… — Gui-Jun Ding, Stephen F. King, Bu-Yao Qu — arXiv: gen sym / arXiv: neutrino

item.title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
item.description: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern-Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux-charge wave packets… — Shengyi Guan, Qiang Jia, Jiahua Tian, Yi-Nan Wang — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Segal's semigroup, Virasoro structure, and Ward identities in Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory
item.description: Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory (CILT for short) is a probabilistically constructed Conformal Field Theory (CFT), expected to have connections to minimal models, Coulomb gas integrals, and loop models. In this paper, we study the quantization of Segal's semigroup given by CILT. Each element $\mathbf T_f$ in the quantized semigroup corresponds to a conformal annulus: the unit disk $\mathbb D$ with $f(\mathbb D^\circ)$ removed, where $f:\mathbb D\to f(\mathbb D)\subset \mathbb D^\circ$ is a contracting… — Yang Xiao, Yuxiao Xie — arXiv: bootstrap

item.title: Holography for integrable field theories
item.description: We develop a holographic dual to the integrable field theories built from $4d$ Chern-Simons theory. The dual theory is a topological string on a generalized Calabi-Yau manifold, which is entirely encoded in a geometric object we call a planar spectral curve. We describe the RG flow for a planar integrable field theory as a geometric flow on the moduli of planar spectral curves. This description is valid at all orders in the 't Hooft coupling. We compute this flow explicitly up to two loops in many examples, and… — Kevin Costello, Joaquin Liniado — arXiv: hodge

item.title: Conformal Bootstrap for surfaces with boundary in Liouville CFT. Part II: spectral resolution and bootstrap
item.description: This paper is the second part of the proof of the conformal bootstrap for Liouville conformal field theory on compact surfaces with boundary. It is devoted to the spectral theory of the half-annulus semigroup and to the resulting bootstrap formula. Building on the Segal axioms and gluing properties established in Part~1~\cite{GRW1}, we identify the generator of the half-annulus semigroup with the boundary Hamiltonian and establish its spectral decomposition by scattering methods. This yields a direct-integral… — Colin Guillarmou, Rémi Rhodes, Baojun Wu — arXiv: bootstrap

item.title: Algebraic Tensor Network Renormalization and Holographic duality
item.description: Emergent generalized symmetries and the holographic principle play very important roles in understanding quantum phase transitions. In recent years, tensor-network renormalization with generalized symmetry and the corresponding fixed-point tensor formulation have been proposed as a discrete spacetime framework for reformulating conformal field theory. Nevertheless, a complete holographic formulation within this framework is still lacking, and the current formulation does not directly accommodate sector partition… — Chenqi Meng, Tian Lan, Zhengcheng Gu — arXiv: gen sym

item.title: Multi-Point Affine Bialgebras for AdS/CFT Integrability
item.description: In this work, we revisit the analytical structure of the classical affine Lie bialgebra underlying the integrable structures of AdS/CFT worldsheet scattering and the one-dimensional Hubbard model. Earlier work showed that the algebraic relations implied two singularity locations in the evaluation parameter plane besides the common expansion points infinity and zero for Laurent polynomials forming the basis for loop and affine algebras. Our aim is to formulate these singularities rigorously using meromorphic… — Niklas Beisert, Egor Im, Hannes Malcha — arXiv: ads cft

item.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
item.description: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup… — Tzu-Chen Huang — arXiv: tqft

item.title: Monopole Catalysis from Standard Model Anomalies
item.description: We study the generalized symmetries associated with Standard Model flavor and their fate in the presence of magnetic monopoles. This illuminates a striking phenomenological consequence: even when baryon and lepton number are classically conserved, the electroweak anomaly induces $ΔB = ΔL \in 3 \mathbb{Z}$ in monopole-fermion scattering for any monopole activating the anomaly. We demonstrate this mechanism in Pati-Salam theory and trinification. — Nathaniel Craig, Dan Sehayek — arXiv: gen sym

item.title: Quantum symmetries and nimreps for an exotic exceptional modular invariant of F4 at level 6
item.description: We revisit an old non-diagonal modular invariant of $F_4$ at level $6$, discovered in 1989. At the time of its discovery, it was noticed that it could not be obtained from a conformal embedding of affine Lie algebras. Later, it was shown that it can be obtained from an extension of a vertex operator algebra which is not of Lie type. To this modular invariant, one can attach a full CFT defined (or formulated) as a module category $\mathcal M$ for the fusion category $\mathcal A = \mathcal C(F_4,6)$. More recently… — Robert Coquereaux — arXiv: tqft

item.title: Exact fillings using universal covers in Floer theory
item.description: We study exact fillings of Legendrians and contact manifolds using Floer theory of universal covers. We prove vanishing results on wrapped Floer homology of the universal cover and symplectic (co)homology with $k[π_1]$ coefficients by using lifted versions of Ritter's TQFT operations. We use these results to show that an exact Maslov zero Lagrangian filling of the standard Legendrian $Λ_{std}$ in any Liouville filling of $(S^{2n-1},ξ_{std})$ is diffeomorphic to a ball in dimension at least 5. We show that the… — Shahnaz Shamim Shahul — arXiv: floer

item.title: Quantum Gravity from Gluing Consistency: AdS/CFT to Spin-Foams
item.description: We argue that BF theory with $SO(d+1,1)$ gauge group provides a SymTFT ''skeleton'' for building AdS$_{d+1}$/CFT$_d$ pairs via gluing consistency as the bootstrap principle, loosely analogous to how compact Chern-Simons theory is a TQFT skeleton for rational CFTs. This is a non-perturbative $bulk$ framework for quantum gravity. The bootstrap is formulated as presentation independence of physical amplitudes within a universal, defect-closed BF sewing calculus, which includes Wilson lines, codimension-two monodromy… — Chethan Krishnan — arXiv: ads cft / arXiv: de sitter

item.title: Peeling off Abelian Anyons and Proliferation Transitions
item.description: We study the invertible one-form global symmetry of a (2+1)-dimensional topological quantum field theory (TQFT). A universal description of this symmetry ``peels off'' all the Abelian anyons from the rest of the TQFT. This allows us to study this symmetry and some of its consequences, independently of the details of the rest of the system. We then describe these Abelian anyons using $\mathrm{U}(1)$ gauge fields with Chern-Simons terms and couple them to a scalar field, thus constructing a particular… — Meng Cheng, Nathan Seiberg — arXiv: tqft

item.title: Anisotropic cosmic birefringence estimates for forthcoming CMB experiments
item.description: Cosmic Birefringence (CB) is a unique probe of physics beyond the Standard Model, potentially sourced by an axion-like field coupled to photons via a Chern-Simons interaction. Recent Planck analyses have strengthened evidence for a non-zero isotropic rotation angle, yet its anisotropic component remains undetected, despite being the key to distinguishing a homogeneous quintessence-like field from spatially varying axion-like dark matter. We forecast the sensitivity of forthcoming ground- and space-based CMB… — Matteo Longo Minnolo, Matteo Billi, Giuseppe Puglisi — arXiv: dark matter

item.title: Compact multi-monopole moduli spaces on Kähler surfaces
item.description: We consider the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations on a 4-manifold in a general setting, where we allow the auxiliary bundle to be non-trivial. We show that when the metric is Kähler and the auxiliary connection is unobstructed anti-self-dual Yang-Mills, the moduli space of solutions is compact for all parameters in some open neighborhood of the given metric and auxiliary connection. We use this fact to compute a count of solutions on some examples of Kähler surfaces. These computations have a surprising… — Ollie Thakar — arXiv: low dim

item.title: Conformal blocks for modular vertex algebras
item.description: Given a vertex operator algebra $V$ over $\mathbb{C}$, it is known how to define so-called sheaves of coinvariants and conformal blocks on the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ of stable, $n$-pointed, genus $g$ curves. We extend this theory to vertex algebras equipped with a notion of change of coordinates over any algebraically closed field. As a by-product of our arguments, we also show that a number of standard assumptions in these constructions can be removed, such as being $C_1$-cofinite or CFT-type. — Colton Griffin — arXiv: tqft

item.title: Photon spheres, elliptic surfaces, and Seiberg-Witten geometry
item.description: We study null geodesics in Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter spacetime and in its $ω=-2/3$ Kiselev deformation through the elliptic curves defined by the radial equation. The relation of these curves to the non-critical $E_7$ Seiberg-Witten family yields differential equations for finite-distance light deflection, and explains the boundary source term through a suitable gauge of the Seiberg-Witten differential. This geometry separates the extremal point $Q^2=M^2$ from the Argyres-Douglas point $Q^2=9M^2/8$. We also… — Cordell Blankenship, Andreas Malmendier, Michael T. Schultz — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Uniqueness of one-phase cones with isolated singularity
item.description: We prove uniqueness of the blow-up at every singular point of the one-phase free boundary problem for which one blow-up has an isolated singularity. The result applies to Lipschitz stationary solutions and does not require any integrability assumption on the cone. In this sense, our result completes the picture for uniqueness of tangent cones at isolated singularities in the one-phase problem. Inspired by Simon's work in the minimal surface setting, we prove an infinite dimensional Łojasiewicz inequality for the… — Matteo Carducci, Bozhidar Velichkov — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Bulk OPE Coefficients of the $E$-Series Virasoro Minimal Models
item.description: We present bulk-primary operator-product coefficients for every Virasoro minimal model with an $E_6$, $E_7$, or $E_8$ modular invariant. Dividing by a universal product of chiral generalized-minimal-model OPE coefficients reduces the conformal bootstrap problem to a finite algebraic problem governed by root-of-unity quantum-group $6j$ symbols. The exceptional factors of the OPE coefficients can be chosen independent of the second Kac indices $s$, and their dependence on the central charge reduces to finitely many… — Amaury Lhoste, Jiaxin Qiao, Masahito Yamazaki — arXiv: bootstrap

item.title: Symmetry-permuting entanglers for non-invertible symmetry-protected topological phases
item.description: 1+1D symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases with invertible symmetry can be characterized by the symmetric entanglers: globally symmetric finite-depth local unitary circuits that generate representative ground states from a product state. For non-invertible symmetries, however, distinct SPT phases, such as the three $\mathrm{Rep}(D_8)$ SPT phases, may not be connected by any symmetric entangler. We show that the three $\mathrm{Rep}(D_8)$ SPT phases can nevertheless be connected by \emph{symmetry-permuting}… — Minyoung You — arXiv: gen sym / arXiv: tqft

item.title: The Zygmund conjecture and Rey's exponential integrability conjecture
item.description: We prove the Zygmund conjecture in all parameters: the maximal operator associated with products of cubes with side lengths $(s_1,\ldots,s_{m-1},φ(s_1,\ldots,s_{m-1}))$, where $φ$ is any positive coordinatewise nondecreasing function, satisfies the weak $L(\log L)^{m-2}$ estimate for every $m\geq3$. The estimate is new for $m>3$. Our approach is to prove Rey's recent conjecture on the exponential integrability of the overlap function $h_{\mathcal G}=\sum_{I\in\mathcal G}\mathbf{1}_I$, with exponent $1/(m-1)$, for… — Henri Martikainen — arXiv: lean

item.title: High-Temperature Vacua of the Standard Model from One-Form Symmetry
item.description: We study the high-temperature vacua of the Standard Model from the perspective of generalized symmetries and the global structure of the gauge group. We analyze the one-loop effective potential for Polyakov loop holonomies, incorporating the gauge identifications induced by gauging discrete subgroups of the electric one-form symmetry. This provides a classification of physically inequivalent vacua for each gauge-group quotient. We further comment on the effects of additional center-charged matter on the residual… — Ling-Xiao Xu — arXiv: gen sym

item.title: More Versions of Real Link Floer Homology
item.description: In this paper, we further develop the real link Floer homology defined by the first author. We introduce a new base-pointing convention that leads to a different version of real link Floer homology and show that this new theory is related to the old one by an exact triangle. We also define a real link Floer theory for multi-based strongly invertible links, which is a strong real Heegaard invariant, and take a first step toward a real link Floer TQFT. A computer implementation for the new theory via grid diagrams… — Yonghan Xiao — arXiv: floer

item.title: Constraints on Axion-like Dark Matter from Cosmic Birefringence with a Polarization Array of Repeating Fast Radio Bursts
item.description: Axion-like dark matter (ALDM) is a well-motivated dark matter candidate whose Chern-Simons coupling to photons can induce cosmic birefringence, producing temporal oscillations and spatial correlation in polarization angle (PA) signals from different sources. Hyperactive repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) with high linear polarization are a particularly promising probe of such signatures. We develop a Bayesian framework to search for PA oscillations caused by ALDM in individual repeating FRBs, and combine multiple… — Xiaohui Liu, Zi-Yan Yuwen, Yun-Long Zhang, Zerui Liu, Shiqian Zhao, Shuai Feng — arXiv: dark matter

item.title: The Gaiotto-Kim Trace Formula and Line Defects
item.description: We study the insertion of 4d half-BPS line defects into the trace formula proposed by Gaiotto and Kim, which computes the ellipsoid partition function of the 3d topological quantum field theory (TQFT) arising from a 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theory. This yields a homomorphism to 3d Wilson loops, preserving the fusion algebra of the 4d defects. We also present a systematic algorithm for determining the simple objects of a 3d TQFT in terms of Wilson loops in the UV 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ abelian… — Sungjoon Kim, Spencer Stubbs — arXiv: tqft

item.title: Affine Harish-Chandra center in positive characteristic
item.description: Let $G$ be a split reductive group defined over a field of characteristic bigger than the Coxeter numbers of its simple factors. We identify the Harish--Chandra centers of the associated Kac--Moody vertex algebras and enveloping algebras at noncritical levels with algebras of functions on moduli spaces of connections for the Langlands dual group $\check{G}$. Namely, given a noncritical level $κ$ for $G$, consider the associated Kac--Moody vertex algebra $V_κ(\mathfrak{g})$ defined on a formal disc $\mathscr{D}$… — Gurbir Dhillon, Ivan Losev — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Cosmological Correlators from Resurgence
item.description: Integrating out heavy particles is generally viewed as an irreversible procedure that erases some physical information above the cutoff scale of the resulting effective theory. However, this does not preclude the possibility of recovering the heavy propagating degrees from the low-energy effective theory with appropriate boundary data supplied. A classic example is the recovery of Schwinger pair production from the resummed Euler-Heisenberg effective action. In this work, we perform a similar exercise in a… — Yuanzhao Li, Zhong-Zhi Xianyu — arXiv: cosmo corr

item.title: Inequalities for 4-Manifolds with Ends using Fibered boundary metric and Seiberg-Witten Equations
item.description: We deduce a new inequality using the Hitchin-Thorpe inequality for noncompact complete four-dimensional manifolds with fibered geometry at infinity and Seiberg-Witten gauge-theoretic techniques. Fibered geometry at infinity is either fibered boundary metric or fibered cusp metric. We prove it for fibered boundary metric when the fiber at boundary is a single point. — Shyamal Kumar Hui, Chandan Kumar Adak — arXiv: low dim

item.title: F-theory on K3 surfaces and orthogonal modular forms
item.description: We identify the precise F-theory backgrounds dual to the heterotic string theory compactified on $T^2$ with general Wilson lines turned on for one of the two $E_8$'s. The elliptic curve describing the backgrounds is expressed in terms of orthogonal modular forms and is determined so that it admits a nontrivial scaling limit yielding a rational elliptic surface. We confirm that the curve reduces to the Seiberg-Witten curve for the E-string theory in this limit. We conjecture that our result gives an explicit… — Kazuhiro Sakai — arXiv: elliptic

item.title: Quasi-algebraic quantization for the B-twist Langlands TQFT
item.description: This is the first part of a program to construct hyperholomorphic families of boundary conditions for the Kapustin--Witten B-twist of the Langlands QFT, otherwise known as \textit{(BBB)-branes}. We define the category of quasi-algebraic sheaves over the Deligne moduli stack, which serves as an analog of the twistor space of Hitchin's moduli stack. This allow us to construct a representation of a simplified version of the Moore--Tachikawa category which is motivated by the relative Langlands program in the sense… — Eric Yen-Yo Chen, Emilio Franco — arXiv: langlands

item.title: Virasoro extensions of generalized Kac-Moody algebras
item.description: Borcherds-Kac-Moody (BKM) Lie algebras are constructed by combining a number of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-s and $3$-dimensional Heisenberg algebras in a certain way, generalizing the celebrated Kac-Moody algebras. Such algebras have a wide range of applications, including the examples of the monster and fake monster Lie algebras being BKM algebras. Among their main features are existence of an invariant bilinear form, denominator identity and Weyl-Kac character formulas for irreducible representations. We introduce a… — Vladyslav Zveryk — arXiv: tqft

item.title: From Closed to Relative Higher-Genus Gromov-Witten Invariants via Resurgent Functions
item.description: Higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of Calabi-Yau threefolds are encoded in a generating function which is an asymptotic series in a formal parameter $λ$. Using resurgence, analytic functions in this formal parameter were uncovered. In this paper we focus on the resolved conifold and study the enumerative meaning of the strong-coupling asymptotic expansion, in powers of $ 1/λ$, of the resurgent analytic functions. We show that this expansion contains both a closed curve-counting contribution in dual variables… — Murad Alim, Noah Tischler — arXiv: floer / arXiv: hodge

item.title: On general background of quantum non-invertible symmetry in 2D
item.description: We study the dual quantum symmetry $\mathrm{Rep}(G)$ in the two-dimensional theory $\widetilde{\mathfrak{T}}_{\mathrm{Rep}(G)}$ obtained by gauging a non-abelian symmetry $G$ of $\mathfrak{T}_G$, where for Lie groups $G$ the gauging is understood as flat gauging. We develop a general framework for computing partition functions of $\widetilde{\mathfrak{T}}_{\mathrm{Rep}(G)}$ in arbitrary non-invertible symmetry backgrounds, represented by topological defect networks of $\mathrm{Rep}(G)$, in terms of the partition… — Jin Chen, Qiang Jia — arXiv: gen sym
